outcome: Pathological colonization of the neonatal gastrointestinal tract
Types of microorganisms colonizing the neonatal gastrointestinal tract
cohort: 94 neonates admitted to a tertiary teaching hospital NICU (51 cases with pathological colonization and 43 controls with normal colonization)
finding: Neonatal exposure to antibiotics was the most significant factor associated with the establishment of pathological microbiota in the neonatal gastrointestinal tract.
mod_finding: Infants born via cesarean section had a higher incidence of pathological colonization.
